mainEntity.name: What does a Singapore Web3 or AI PR program actually cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seven workstreams. One: Singapore exclusive lead with The Business Times, DealStreetAsia, Channel News Asia, The Straits Times or e27 depending on the audience. Two: Singapore re-report wave across Tech in Asia, Tech Wire Asia, Asia Tech Daily and Lianhe Zaobao (for Chinese-language Singapore audiences) timed to lift inside the same day as the exclusive. Three: international tier-1 re-report through CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, AI Magazine or TechCrunch 24 hours behind the Singapore lift. Four: MAS-aware framing baked into every press copy under the 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime and the upcoming stablecoin legislation. Five: named regional KOL voices on X, YouTube and Telegram with FTC-and-MAS-aware briefs. Six: on-ground event leverage at Token2049 Singapore (Marina Bay Sands, October 2026) and the Singapore FinTech Festival. Seven: founder LinkedIn and X-Asia activation timed to the press cycle.

mainEntity.name: How much does Singapore Web3 or AI PR cost in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three commercial models. Singapore Quarterly Retainer runs 5,000 to 11,000 US dollars per month over three to six months and covers one to two named-Singapore placements per quarter plus the international re-report wave. Singapore Single-Market Launch Sprint runs 10,000 to 28,000 US dollars total for one focused 14 to 21 day window timed to a MAS announcement, Token2049 keynote, Project Guardian milestone or a Series A or B raise. Always-On Singapore Coordinator runs 2,800 US dollars per month with a three-month minimum. KOL fees sit on top. Published 2026 Southeast Asia KOL rates run nano 250 to 1,800 US dollars per deliverable, micro 700 to 6,000, mid 8,000 to 25,000, macro 20,000 to 80,000 plus, with a Token2049 event-week premium of 30 to 50 percent on every tier.

mainEntity.name: Why does Singapore press want the MAS framing inside the first three paragraphs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because Singapore business press treats the regulator as a participant in the story, not a backdrop. The Business Times and Channel News Asia read every Web3 announcement against the 2026 Digital Token Service Provider regime, the upcoming stablecoin legislation, Project Guardian institutional partners and the wholesale CBDC tokenised-bill settlement track. Press copy that buries the regulator paragraph reads as either uninformed or evasive. Conversely, press copy that opens with the right MAS frame signals founder-credibility before any product detail. The Singapore FinTech Festival announcement cycle every November is the most-watched MAS calendar moment globally.

mainEntity.name: How does Token2049 Singapore change the press calendar for a Web3 founder?

acceptedAnswer.text: Token2049 Singapore on 7 and 8 October 2026 at Marina Bay Sands is the world's largest crypto conference and the single highest-leverage week for a Web3 launch in APAC. The press cycle starts five weeks out with embargo briefings to The Business Times, DealStreetAsia and Channel News Asia, lifts on the Monday before the event with a Singapore exclusive, runs side-events and named-byline coverage through the conference and closes with a post-event tier-1 international re-report on the Friday. Token2049 week press demand outstrips supply by 4 to 5x, which is why the briefings start in mid-August and not early September.

mainEntity.name: Does Singapore PR earn AI search citations on regional queries?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Singapore audiences searching in English and Mandarin see a mix of Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude responses on Web3, AI and fintech queries. Named-byline placements in The Business Times, Channel News Asia, DealStreetAsia, e27 and Lianhe Zaobao carry the named-expertise and E-E-A-T signal Google explicitly names in its AI optimization guide. The Princeton GEO study (Aggarwal et al., arXiv:2311.09735) found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines, and the dynamic holds for Singapore-English and Singapore-Mandarin AI search queries on best Web3 PR agency Singapore, MAS stablecoin licence and Token2049 announcement.

mainEntity.name: Which Singapore outlets are the right exclusives for an AI startup versus a Web3 startup?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an AI startup with an enterprise customer announcement, The Business Times or Channel News Asia for the customer-name framing. For an AI startup raising a Series A or B, DealStreetAsia for the funding lead with e27 and Tech in Asia as same-day re-reports. For a Web3 startup announcing a MAS Digital Token Service Provider in-principle approval or licence, The Business Times for the regulatory lead with Cointelegraph and CoinDesk Asia re-reports 24 hours behind. For a Web3 startup launching a Token2049 keynote, an embargoed DealStreetAsia exclusive five days ahead followed by the international tier-1 re-report timed to the keynote. For a Project Guardian institutional partner story, Channel News Asia or The Business Times for the institutional-partner-name lead.

mainEntity.name: Does Shilika work with Singapore-domiciled founders who actually operate in another region?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A meaningful share of Singapore-domiciled Web3 founders run the operating team out of India, Vietnam, Korea or the US. The Singapore PR programme works the same way: Singapore exclusive for the MAS-and-fund-raise framing, then a home-team region re-report wave timed behind it. The brief simply names the operating geography as a credibility anchor (Indian engineering bench, Korean exchange listing pipeline, Vietnamese retail traction) rather than burying it in the bio.
